cs_jordan: FYI customer Acme (ticket #12345) reporting a sustained throughput drop on Dedicated pool redwood-eu-2 since ~03:18 UTC. Seeing 503s and p95 latency up to 8-10s. Token throughput ~4x lower than baseline. Logs attached.

support_jess: Copy — pinging @eng_oncall_mike and @runtime_sre_ana, escalating to eng.

eng_oncall_mike: Oncall here. Any deploys or autoscale events around that time? Any recent config changes to schedulers or batching?

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: deploy redwood/serve 3.14.0 -> prod-eu at 03:10 UTC (commit abc123)

runtime_sre_ana: Looking now. Can you paste recent queue metrics (avg batch size, tokens per batch, inflight, queue_len) and the pool config? Need to understand if this is packing/quantum related.

customer_acme_infra: Sharing partial logs from their side:
```
[03:18:12] request_id=Z1 status=503 latency_ms=1205
[03:18:13] avg_batch_size=1.1 avg_tokens_per_batch=18 inflight=48 queue_len=230
[03:18:14] worker_idle=0 prefill_ms=240
```
They also reported lots of small bursty requests from their autocomplete clients. Throughput dropped ~4x.

eng_oncall_mike: avg_batch_size=1.1 is a red flag. Continuous batching is not aggregating. Could be scheduler quantum too low or pack window disabled. Any noisy tenants on that pool?

support_jess: Acme confirms a traffic pattern change: many parallel tiny requests starting ~03:15, not a single large stream.

runtime_sre_ana: Please run admin dump for queue stats: 
```
curl -sS -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN' http://internal-admin/redwood/eu-2/queue_stats
```
and paste output. Need pool scheduler_policy, quantum, max_batch_tokens, prefill flag, prefix cache hit rate.

eng_oncall_mike: Also check autoscale events: `kubectl get hpa -n redwood-eu-2` and `kubectl describe hpa redwood-runtime`.

support_jess: Admin output pasted:
```
connection_pool: dedicated-eu-2
avg_batch_size: 1.08
median_latency_ms: 980
max_batch_tokens: 1024
token_budget_per_window: 200000
scheduler_policy: round-robin-quantum=16ms
prefill_enabled: true
prefix_cache_hit: 5%
```

runtime_sre_ana: That explains it — scheduler quantum=16ms + prefill true + very low prefix cache hit means the runtime is prioritizing latency and pushing tiny batches through instead of waiting to pack. For a tenant with many small requests that reduces throughput and increases throttling. Two quick levers: increase quantum (pack window) to 40-60ms or switch to `pack-first` scheduler so requests can fill before dispatch. Also consider bumping `max_batch_tokens` or token budget for this tenant if autoscale can't catch up.

eng_oncall_mike: I can hotpatch the pool to try `scheduler_policy=pack-first,quantum=50ms` for Acme's tenant and monitor. Rolling that now. If that doesn't help, we can move them to a dedicated isolated pool to avoid noisy neighbor effects.

deploy-bot: config-change: pool:europe-2 update by mike at 03:30 UTC — scheduler_policy -> pack-first, quantum=50ms

customer_acme_infra: Testing now... initial results look much better. Latency p95 down to 220-400ms, avg_batch_size=5.2, throughput back to ~85% of baseline. No more 503s in the last 2 minutes.

cs_jordan: :thumbsup: I'll update the ticket with the workaround and timeline. We should still investigate root cause — why quantum was 16ms in the first place and why the default changed.

runtime_sre_ana: Action items: 1) Reproduce locally with a microburst traffic generator using current scheduler parameters and confirm pack-first fixes it. 2) Add a telemetry alert: avg_batch_size < 2 for > 5 minutes -> page. 3) Audit recent deploys for changes to scheduler defaults (search commits between 3.13.8..3.14.0). 4) Consider tenant-aware defaults: if prefix_cache_hit < 10% and observed request size < X, prefer pack-first.

eng_oncall_mike: I'll run the repro and open an incident follow-up. ETA ~2h.

support_jess: Noted. I'll tell Acme we're monitoring and will keep ticket open until we validate sustained recovery.

cs_jordan: Thanks everyone — nice triage. :eyes:
